_doc: Age-defining crises (src/systems/crises.js): rare world events that run for years in phases — an invasion from beyond the map's edge, a great plague along the trade roads, a schism of a faith, a famine decade, a gold rush. One at a time: after one ends the world rests gapYears before the next may begin (2–4 a century). Every roll is a hash of the world seed and the crisis (never the shared RNG). Times are in years of Seasons.DAYS_PER_YEAR days unless named *Days. Phrase lists are picked by hash; {tokens} are filled by the system.

peoples.name: the Pale Fleet
peoples.from: beyond the edge of the charts

peoples.name: the Iron Brotherhood
peoples.from: the mountains past the world's rim

omens: Fishermen and shepherds tell of strange fires and sails off {edge}: {people} are coming from {from}.
wave: Another fleet of {people} came ashore near {edge}, {strength} strong.
landing: {people} have landed near {edge}: {hosts} hosts, {strength} strong, march on {target}.
alliance: Against them {members} swear the Grand Alliance and lay down their quarrels.
founded: {people} proclaimed {realm} at {town}: the invaders mean to stay.
refounded: The {realm} rose again at {town}: the invaders would not be driven out.
settled: The invaders' hosts laid down their arms in {realm}; peace was made and {realm} took its place among the realms.
reland: The fleet took {host} aboard and put it ashore again within sight of {town}.
withdrew: Having won no foothold, {people} took to their ships and sailed home.
repelled: The last of {people} were driven out, and the {realm} was no more.

start: {name} came ashore at {town} with a ship's crew from abroad.
return: {name} came back with the spring, ashore at {town}.
waning: {name} began to burn out, leaving {towns} towns stricken.
end: {name} passed at last; some {dead} souls lay dead in {towns} towns, and fields stood untended for want of hands.

dispute: {reformer} of {town} preached against the masters of {faith}, and crowds came to hear.
split: The faithful of {faith} split: {reformed} broke from the old church, and its preachers crossed every border.
war: {a} and {b} went to war over the true faith.
triumph: {side} prevailed in the end, and the crowns that had stood against it bowed to the faith of {winner}.
triumphOld: The new church was broken: {reformed} was driven back into hiding, and its crowns returned to their old faiths.
peace: The Peace of the Faiths: {reformed} and {orthodox} each kept their own, uneasily.

start: The rains failed over {region}, and the granaries of {realms} began to empty.
year: Another year of blight and empty barns in {region}.
end: The harvests came back to {region} after {years} hungry years.

start: Gold was struck in the hills by {town}: a mother lode.
rush: Thousands came to dig at {town}; it swelled to {pop} souls.
bust: The gold of {town} ran thin and the diggers drifted away.
end: {name} was over; {town} kept {kept} of its newcomers.
